title: Optimized measles virus glycoprotein-pseudotyped lentiviral vector production for human B cells
author: Vamva, Ozog, et al.
materials: One Shot™ Stbl3™ Chemically Competent E. coli
EasySep Human B cell Isolation Kit

3rd generation lentiviral vectors are made of 4 independent plasmids coding for the transfer vector, the packaging constructs and the envelope. The following steps ensure transfection-grade production of plasmid constructs.1.Transform different vials of One Shot™ Stbl3™ Chemically Competent E. coli cells with 10 ng of pCG-HΔ24, pCG-FΔ30, pMDLg/RRE, pRSV-Rev, p-MND-eGFP-eCD4-Ig (or the transfer vector of interest) following the manufacturer’s protocol (https://www.thermofisher.com/document-connect/document-connect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.thermofisher.com%2FTFS-Assets%2FLSG%2Fmanuals%2Foneshot_stbl3_man.pdf).Note: This E. coli strain is recommended for use when working with sequences containing direct repeats, including lentiviral transfer vector DNA.2.16 h later, pick up a single colony from each transformation plate and inoculate into a 250 mL ampLB medium (see materials and equipment) in a 1 L flask. Cover the top of the flask with foil and create small holes with a 20 or 200 uL pipet tip. Incubate the flask at 37°C with constant shaking (300 rpm) for 16 h overnight.CRITICAL: The concentration and quality of plasmid DNA are very critical parameters to achieve high transfection efficiencies, especially in a protocol that requires the co-transfection of 5 independent plasmids. Yield and quality of plasmid DNA depend, amongst other parameters, on the bacterial host strain and on the growth conditions. Low bacterial growth will inevitably lead to low plasmid yield, while culture overgrowing can lead to a higher percentage of dead or starving cells, resulting in potentially degraded or contaminated plasmid DNA. Create holes on the surface of each flask and use 1L flasks (four times the volume of the culture) to maintain LB saturated with oxygen.3.16 h later collect and load the culture in a centrifuge tube. Spin at 4,000×g for 30 min at 4°C.4.Resuspend the bacterial pellet in 12 mL of Resuspension Buffer RES+RNase A by pipetting the cells up and down and vortex to ensure sample homogeneity.5.Add 12 mL of lysis buffer, LYS (ensure that lysis buffer is not precipitated), to the bacterial lysate and mix by gently inverting the tube 5 times. Incubate at room temperature (RT=22°C–24°C) for 5 min.CRITICAL: Ensure gentle mixing of the culture to prevent membrane shear that can result to bacterial chromosomal DNA release contaminating the plasmid DNA suspension.6.Meanwhile apply 12 mL of equilibration buffer EQU onto the rim of the NucleoBond® Xtra Column Filter to ensure high yield.7.Neutralize the lysis buffer by adding 12 mL of buffer NEU. Mix thoroughly until the lysate is colorless. Load lysate on the NucleoBond® Xtra Column Filter.8.Add 10 mL of Wash Buffer EQU. Once this step is complete, discard the Column Filter and perform another wash step by adding 12 mL of EQU buffer.9.Place the column in a sterile 50 mL falcon tube. Elute plasmid DNA with 5 mL of pre-warmed Elution buffer ELU.10.Precipitate eluted plasmid DNA with 3.5 mL of isopropanol and thorough mixing. Centrifuge at 4,500 × g for 1 h. Alternatively, add the isopropanol to the elution column, to simultaneously increase the yield of plasmid DNA.11.Decant supernatant and add 10 mL of 70% ethanol. Wash the pellet by resuspending it in 70% ethanol and ultracentrifuge as above. Remove supernatant and allow pellet to air dry at RT for 10 min.CRITICAL: Resuspend the pellet in ethanol and run an hour long precipitation step to increase the quality for transfection grade plasmid DNA.12.Dissolve DNA pellet in 500 μL of sterile water. Quantify and qualify plasmid DNA with UV spectrometry and evaluate by restriction digests, respectively. Aliquot plasmid DNA to avoid multiple rounds of freeze-thawing and store in −20°C up to 2 years.CRITICAL: Ensure the quality of plasmid DNA by measuring the 260/230 ratio. Generally, a ratio close to 2.0 is considered pure. Following this protocol the expected yield is ≥2 μg/mL. High plasmid concentrations and plasmid supercoiling are important parameters to achieve high transfection efficiency. Do not proceed if your concentration is less than ∼1.5 μg/mL.

Timing: 1.5 h
76.Collect and centrifuge all activated human primary B cells for 5 min at 300 × g at RT. VCN should be measured at 7–11 days post transduction to ensure degradation of non-integrated provirus (Figure 3).
CRITICAL: It is important to collect all primary B cells for gDNA extraction. As mentioned above, one of the limitations of the in vitro culture of human primary B cells is the high death rate. Extraction of gDNA from a small number of B cells of which approximately 50% are expected to be dead will lead to an overestimation of VCN due to DNA degradation. Therefore, it is of paramount importance to use the maximum number of B cells possible.
77.Resuspend pellet in 200 μL PBS and proceed to gDNA extraction using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue kit (Qiagen).78.Add 20 μL proteinase K and 200 μL of Buffer AL. Mix thoroughly by vortexing and incubate samples at 56°C for 10 min for efficient cell lysis.79.Add 200 μL pure ethanol and mix the sample thoroughly by vortexing. Pipet the sample into a DNeasy Mini spin column placed in a 2 mL collection tube and centrifuge at ≥6,000 × g for 1 min at RT. Discard the flow-through and return the spin column to the same collection tube.80.Add 500 μL of Buffer AW1 in the spin column and centrifuge as above.81.Add 500 μL Buffer AW2 in the spin column and centrifuge for 3 min at 20,000 × g at RT. Discard the collection tube.82.Transfer the spin column to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. Elute the DNA by adding 50 μL of water to the center of the spin column membrane. Incubate for 5 min at RT. Centrifuge for 1 min at ≥ 6,000 × g at RT and proceed to nanodrop.
CRITICAL: Elute DNA in 50 μl of water. Manufacturer’s protocol suggests a 200 μl final volume, however due to the small number of live B cells with intact chromosomal DNA, addition of a a high elution volume can lead to diluted gDNA concentrations that will not suffice for the subsequent digital droplet PCR (ddPCR) reaction. Elution of DNA in a volume smaller than 50 μl will be inadequate for sufficient membrane hydration and will also lead to small gDNA concentrations. Following this protocol you should expect to get a gDNA concentration of 10–50 ng/ml. Do not proceed to the next step unless can see a distinct 260 nm peak of ≥10 ng/mL gDNA.

steps.title: Prepare plasmid DNA for transfection
steps.instruction: Generate high‑quality, transfection‑grade plasmid DNA for all five lentiviral components using a Stbl3 bacterial host and a NucleoBond Xtra column.

substeps.instruction: Transform One Shot™ Stbl3™ chemically competent E. coli with 10 ng of each plasmid (pCG‑HΔ24, pCG‑FΔ30, pMDLg/RRE, pRSV‑Rev, p‑MND‑eGFP‑eCD4‑Ig or alternative transfer vector) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

After 16 h, pick a single colony from each plate and inoculate into 250 mL ampicillin‑LB medium in a 1 L flask; cover with foil, puncture holes with a 20‑200 µL tip, and incubate at 37 °C, 300 rpm for 16 h.
Harvest culture by centrifugation at 4,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the bacterial pellet in 12 mL Resuspension Buffer RES + RNase A, pipetting up/down and vortexing for homogeneity.
Add 12 mL Lysis Buffer LYS (ensure it is not precipitated), invert gently 5 times, and incubate at room temperature (22‑24 °C) for 5 min.
Apply 12 mL Equilibration Buffer EQU onto the rim of a NucleoBond® Xtra Column Filter.
Add 12 mL Neutralization Buffer NEU, mix until the lysate becomes colorless, and load the lysate onto the column.
Wash the column with 10 mL EQU, discard the column, then wash again with 12 mL EQU.
Place the column in a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube and elute plasmid DNA with 5 mL pre‑warmed Elution Buffer ELU.
Precipitate the eluate by adding 3.5 mL isopropanol, mix thoroughly, and centrifuge at 4,500 × g for 1 h (or add isopropanol directly to the column to increase yield).
Decant the supernatant, add 10 mL 70 % ethanol, resuspend the pellet in ethanol, ultracentrifuge as above, discard supernatant, and air‑dry the pellet at room temperature for 10 min.

Dissolve the DNA pellet in 500 µL sterile water, measure concentration and purity (260/230 ≈ 2.0) by UV spectrometry, confirm ≥1.5 µg/mL (expected ≥2 µg/mL), aliquot, and store at –20 °C for up to 2 years.

steps.title: Isolate and activate primary B cells
steps.instruction: Recover frozen PBMCs, enrich for B cells using the EasySep kit, and seed them in expansion medium at the proper density.

substeps.instruction: Thaw one vial of isolated PBMCs in a 37 °C water bath; the starting concentration should be 130–150 × 10⁶ cells/mL.
Add 5 mL of the PBMC suspension slowly and dropwise to 20 mL PBS.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min at room temperature and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 mL PBS, repeat the 400 × g 5 min spin, and count the cells.
Aspirate the supernatant and add EasySep buffer up to 8.5 mL as recommended by the manufacturer.
Transfer the total volume to a 14 mL polystyrene round‑bottom tube, add 50 µL enrichment cocktail per mL of sample, and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Vortex the magnetic beads for 30 s, then add 75 µL magnetic beads per mL of sample and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Add up to 5 mL EasySep buffer, place the tube in the magnet, and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Invert the magnet, pour the enriched B‑cell suspension into a new sterile tube.
Count the enriched B cells and resuspend them in B‑cell expansion medium at 1.5 × 10⁶ cells/mL, using a final volume of 3–5 mL per well of a 6‑well plate.

steps.title: Stain B cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Perform extracellular and intracellular staining to assess transduction efficiency and B‑cell phenotype.

substeps.instruction: On day 7, count cells and transfer 2 × 10⁵ B cells per condition into a 96‑well round‑bottom plate; add 100 µL PBS and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Decant supernatant, add 200 µL PBS, and repeat the spin.
Prepare extracellular staining master mix in PBS: AF350 LIVE/DEAD™ fixable violet (1:1000), Brilliant Violet 605 anti‑human CD19 (1:200), Brilliant Violet 785 anti‑human CD3 (1:200).
Add 50 µL extracellular master mix to each well, pipette up/down, and incubate at 4 °C for 30 min in the dark.
Add 200 µL PBS, centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min, and discard supernatant.
Add 100 µL Cytofix/Cytoperm™ fixation‑permeabilization solution, mix gently, and incubate at room temperature for 20 min in the dark.
Add 200 µL Perm/Wash™ Buffer, centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min; repeat this wash once more.
Add 100 µL Cytoperm™ Permeabilization Buffer Plus, incubate at 4 °C for 10 min in the dark.
Add 200 µL Perm/Wash™, spin, and repeat the wash.
Add 100 µL Cytofix/Cytoperm™ solution again, incubate at room temperature for 5 min in the dark.
Add 200 µL Perm/Wash™, spin, and repeat the wash.
Prepare intracellular staining master mix: PE/Cyanine7 anti‑human IgM (1:200) diluted in Perm/Wash™.
Add 50 µL intracellular master mix, pipette, and incubate at 4 °C for 30 min in the dark.
Prepare compensation beads by mixing 3 drops positive beads, 3 drops negative beads, and 1 µL of each antibody used; keep at 4 °C for 30 min in the dark.
Add 200 µL Perm/Wash™, centrifuge, and repeat the wash.
Decant supernatant and resuspend the stained cells in 250 µL PBS; proceed to acquisition on a flow cytometer.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA from B cells
steps.instruction: Isolate high‑quality gDNA from the activated B‑cell culture for downstream vector copy number analysis.

substeps.instruction: Collect all activated B cells and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 µL PBS.
Add 20 µL proteinase K and 200 µL Buffer AL (Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue kit), vortex thoroughly, and incubate at 56 °C for 10 min.
Add 200 µL absolute ethanol, vortex to mix, and transfer the lysate to a DNeasy Mini spin column placed in a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge at ≥6,000 × g for 1 min at room temperature; discard the flow‑through and return the column to the collection tube.
Add 500 µL Buffer AW1, centrifuge as above and discard flow‑through.
Add 500 µL Buffer AW2, centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 3 min at room temperature, and discard the collection tube.

Transfer the spin column to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 50 µL nuclease‑free water to the center of the membrane, incubate at room temperature for 5 min, then centrifuge at ≥6,000 × g for 1 min to elute DNA.
Measure DNA concentration (expect 10–50 ng/µL) and verify a 260 nm peak ≥10 ng/µL before proceeding.
Perform vector copy number (VCN) measurement by digital droplet PCR 7–11 days post‑transduction.

description: This protocol describes the development of a Measles virus envelope gp pseudotyped (MV) lentiviral vector (MV-LV) production system which can be used to package complex transgene containing lentiviral vectors. We chose to evaluate the pMND-eGFP-eCD4-Ig lentiviral vector, a bicistronic vector that contains eGFP (Tsien, 1998) and the HIV-1 entry inhibitor immunoadhesin eCD4-Ig (Gardner et al., 2015), under the control of the constitutive MND (myeloproliferative sarcoma virus enhancer, negative control region deleted, dl587rev primer-binding site substituted) promoter (herein referred to as MND-eGFP-eCD4-Ig and described in key resources table). This transfer vector serves as a model for larger lentiviral bicistronic vectors which have been associated with reduced LV titers (Kumar et al., 2001; Morgan et al., 2019). We outline the steps to prepare high-titer MV-LV to transduce human primary B cells, a cell target important for gene therapy applications of therapeutic potential, including the treatment of genetic diseases (Hung et al., 2018), infectious diseases (Moffett et al., 2019; Nahmad et al., 2020), auto-immune disorders (Greiner et al., 2019), cancers (Page et al., 2020), and the possible use of chimeric B cell receptors (Pesch et al., 2019). The eCD4-Ig gene was chosen for use given the expressed protein has antibody-like properties, suitable for B cell expression studies, and to ensure that MV-LVs encoding complex expression cassettes can also achieve high transduction efficiencies in human primary B cells. To improve MV-LV titers, we used the CD46KO 293T cell line (Ozog et al., 2019) which prevents cell membrane fusion when MV is expressed due to the loss of CD46 required for measles binding and entry and the resulting death of transfected producer cells (Figure 1).
